messages:
lina: heads up — after we swapped in the quantized reranker v2 for the holdout run, overall NDCG@10 fell ~4 points but MRR barely moved. unclear if this is real or an eval mismatch. anyone seen this pattern?

derek: mm — do you have the eval command + seed? sometimes tokenizer mismatch or truncation changes doc passages and hits ndcg more than mrr. :thinking_face:

lina: sure — run we used:```bash
python eval/rerank_eval.py --model rerank-v2-q4 --dataset webqa_holdout.jsonl --split test --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42 --truncate-doc 512
```

emma: can you paste the top-level numbers? also did you change the query normalization (lowercase/punct) or templates? small query differences can reorder top-k which affects ndcg more.

lina: baseline (fp16) -> NDCG@10: 0.672, MRR: 0.481
quantized -> NDCG@10: 0.634, MRR: 0.478
so MRR ~ stable, ndcg down ~4pts

rajesh: two quick checks: 1) ensure the tokenizer/vocab used at encode time is identical (subword offsets can shift passages). 2) check doc chunking boundaries — if you changed `--truncate-doc` that can bias against longer relevant passages.

eva: also try computing bootstrap CI for ndcg to see if change is significant. small ndcg drops can be within noise depending on eval set size. we have a small helper:```bash
python eval/bootstrap_ci.py --metric ndcg@10 --runs 1000 --seed 0 --preds preds_quant.jsonl --gold holdout_labels.jsonl
```

lina: ran bootstrap quick: quantized ndcg@10 95% CI [0.628,0.640], fp16 ndcg@10 95% CI [0.667,0.677] — non overlapping. so seems real.

derek: interesting. two more things to isolate: A) rerun with identical tokenization pipeline by precomputing encoded features and comparing logits. B) run per-query delta to see if the drop concentrates on long documents or specific query templates. e.g.,```
python eval/per_query_delta.py --preds1 preds_fp16.jsonl --preds2 preds_q.jsonl --out deltas.csv
```

emma: addendum: check whether listwise losses respond differently than pairwise during quantization. we onboarded a listwise-trained reranker; quantization might degrade the softmax tail more and change rank order for lower-relevance docs which hurts ndcg.

rajesh: good point. also verify eval metric implementation — we had a past bug where ndcg normalization used top-5 ideal instead of top-10 when there were ties, causing subtle shifts. ci-bot: can you link the metric impl commit?

ci-bot: linked metrics impl: https://ci.internal/repo/metrics/commit/3f8a4b (note: commit includes fix for ndcg ideal_k bug) :white_check_mark:

lina: checked metric impl; we're on latest. next steps I propose: 1) precompute tokens using `tokenize.py` from model repo for both fp16 and q runs and re-run scoring 2) rerun with `--truncate-doc 256` and `--truncate-doc 1024` to see sensitivity 3) produce per-query delta and aggregate by query length/template 4) try symmetric quantization config q5 to see gradation.

derek: sounds good. I can take (1) and (3) today. emma will try q5. rajesh can look at loss/architecture sensitivity. leave notes in the PR so we record which config found the regression. :thumbsup:

emma: quick note — when you do per-query delta, group by `query_template` field in dataset (we added those tags last quarter) so we can see template-level regressions instead of raw length only.

lina: will do. will post back with deltas + small heatmap. thanks all :rocket:
